feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: Explore scientific breakthroughs, space discoveries, research trends and everyday mysteries with NPR’s science team. Plus episodes from the Short Wave podcast.

entry.title: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts
entry.summary: Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions.

entry.title: Time expert Philippe Richard on why scientists are changing how we keep time
entry.summary: Scientists have voted to change how the world keeps time, but most people won't even notice. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Philippe Richard, director of Switzerland's Federal Institute of Metrology.

entry.title: The latest in space science: We look back at the Big Bang
entry.summary: In this edition of Spacing Out, the team from Short Wave shares the latest developments in space science, including the theory on why the universe is made of matter

entry.title: Should 'bird brain' be a compliment? Here's how crows think fast
entry.summary: New research in the journal Science finds that crows turn visual information into decisions twice as fast as humans and primates. They also process information is quite similarly to humans.

entry.title: New human data hints at psychedelics' potential to combat inflammation
entry.summary: Lab studies have shown that psychedelics like psilocybin can lower inflammation and may be protective for a range of illnesses. Now, researchers are publishing some of the first data in humans that signals this holds potential for patients with neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease.

entry.title: How much does pregnancy cost? Be prepared with these tips
entry.summary: The cost of having a baby is difficult to predict. The amount families pay varies widely. Here are five tips to help you prepare for the often unexpected costs of pregnancy and giving birth.

entry.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
entry.summary: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.

entry.title: What time is it on the moon?
entry.summary: James Olthoff, a delegate to the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, talks to NPR's Joel Rose about why it's important to accurately measure time on the moon.

entry.title: Dozens of critically endangered orangutans rescued from Indonesian wildfires
entry.summary: Rescuers in Indonesia have saved dozens of orangutans from wildfires. The critically endangered species is fighting for their lives and habitats during this deadly wildfire season.

entry.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment
entry.summary: For the first time since 2014, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidelines for the treatment of symptoms commonly associated with menopause.
